title: Why Drains Gurgle: Understanding Negative Pressure and Venting
description: A gurgling drain is a classic sign of a venting issue within a drainage system. When wastewater flows down a pipe, it pushes air ahead of it and pulls air behind it. Without a properly sized and unobstructed plumbing vent, this movement creates negative pressure—a vacuum effect. The system attempts to equalize this pressure by pulling air through the nearest trap, sucking out the liquid seal and causing a gurgling noise. Over time, a siphoned trap lets harmful sewer gases escape into the building. Identifying whether the issue is a clogged vent pipe or inadequate venting design is essential for restoring smooth flow and indoor air quality.

Identifying whether the issue is a clogged vent pipe or inadequate venting design is essential for restoring smooth flow and indoor air quality.
